name: TPG Angelo Gordon
summary: TPG's land bank is 'TPG Essential Housing' (EHF), run out of TPG Credit Solutions in New York with a Scottsdale asset-management arm (AGWIP Asset Management, Steve Benson); the Angelo Gordon name is being dropped from the product. By its own count (Jan 2026) it has originated 850+ projects, $22bn+ of project value and about 150,000 homesites since 2020 for 16 builders in 24 states, about 40% of it in California, with zero losses claimed; Lennar is the anchor under a first-look arrangement dating from an Oct 2020 master agreement. It sells one product: short-duration, close-to-production land (option term under 40 months, first takedown inside about 10 months), a 19.9%-20% non-refundable deposit, fixed monthly takedowns with no slippage, builder completion guarantee and a put-back right, and it says it competes by being the biggest and cheapest rather than by taking longer or riskier land. Fund IV held a $2bn first close in Q3 2026 toward a $3bn+ target (SBCERA $150m, TCDRS $200m, Kern $50m) and aims at about $13bn of originations over 30 months, so expect it to be pricing aggressively for finished-lot and late-stage deals through early 2029. Entity names in county records ('TPG AG EHC III (ticker) Multi State n, LLC') point to Meritage, New Home, Landsea, Hovnanian and Century alongside Lennar and Toll, and a late-2025 deal with private regional builder Schuber Mitchell suggests it is moving down-market. Its option rate, lenders and fund-level debt terms are not public.

facts.fact: On TPG's Q3 2026 earnings call (29 Oct 2026) CEO Jon Winkelried said TPG held a $2 billion first close for its fourth Essential Housing fund, already larger than the predecessor fund, and described the strategy as providing 'bespoke land financing to leading homebuilders'. CFO said Q4 2026 fundraising would include further Essential Housing capital. Source is a third-party transcript copy of the call.
facts.source_title: TPG Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (Earnings Whispers copy)

facts.fact: IPE Real Assets (13 Nov 2026): TPG Essential Housing Fund IV first close $2bn against a target of at least $3bn; no timetable for final close; named LPs SBCERA ($150m) and Kern County ERA ($50m). The prior fund (Fund III) reached a final close of $1.62bn in 2024.
facts.source_title: IPE Real Assets: TPG's US residential credit fund secures $2bn in first close

facts.fact: Texas County & District Retirement System committed $200m to TPG Essential Housing IV (target $3bn of equity), reported 23 Sep 2026; Kern County ERA committed $50m in Aug 2026.
facts.source_title: IREI: TCDRS commits $200m to TPG Essential Housing IV

facts.fact: SBCERA board approved $150m to the then-unlaunched TPG Essential Housing Fund 4 (reported 27 Mar 2026): target at least $3bn, first close expected July 2026, 30-month period to deploy capital; strategy described as short-term financing of construction-ready land kept off homebuilder balance sheets.
facts.source_title: IPE Real Assets: SBCERA commits $150m to TPG's latest US housing fund

facts.fact: Fund III (TPG AG Essential Housing Fund III) was marketed in 2024 with a $3bn target including a $500m contribution from the manager, a 13%-15% target net IRR, and had raised $1.3bn by end of June 2024; Kern County ERA committed $50m (Aug 2024) and classed it as core. Compare the later-reported $1.62bn final close (2024).
facts.source_title: IPE Real Assets: KCERA commits to TPG Angelo Gordon's US housing debt fund

facts.fact: The founding document of the Lennar program is public: Master Agreement dated 8 Oct 2020 between AG Essential Housing Company 1, L.P. (Owner; GP AG Essential Housing GP, LLC; manager Angelo, Gordon & Co., L.P.) and Lennar's Essential Housing Financing, LLC, with Lennar Corporation joining as Parent. It set up the 'SPV-1 Program' with Owner equity capped at $1,000m during the investment period. Each admitted property gets an Option Agreement, Construction Agreement and a parent-level Termination Fee Agreement; lot prices are set to produce a 'Target Return' (the rate is on Schedule 1, not in the filed text read); a 'Pause Rate' monthly fee applies if takedowns are paused. New York law.
facts.source_title: Lennar FY2020 10-K, Exhibit 10.12 (Master Agreement, AG Essential Housing Company 1, L.P.)

facts.fact: The 2020 Lennar Master Agreement shows how the platform is organised: notices go to the Owner c/o AGWIP Asset Management LLC, 8585 E. Hartford Drive, Suite 118, Scottsdale, AZ (attn. Steven S. Benson), with copy to Angelo, Gordon & Co. in New York (attn. Bryan Rush). Signed for the Owner by Gregory Shalette as authorized signatory. AGWIP is the Scottsdale asset manager, AG New York is the investment manager.
facts.source_title: Lennar FY2020 10-K, Exhibit 10.12

facts.fact: Hunterbrook (31 Mar 2026), citing SBCERA pitch materials and a 2024 SBCERA presentation video: on the Lennar land bank AG takes a 19.9% upfront deposit (treated as first loss; roughly twice Millrose's 10%), a maximum 40-month term with a fixed monthly takedown schedule, a right to terminate, keep the deposit and resell improved lots if Lennar falls behind, plus a termination fee. AG managing director Bryan Rush told SBCERA in 2024 there is 'really no flexibility' in the schedule. AG reported a 15% IRR on its first Lennar land bank. The option rate itself is not disclosed; Hunterbrook thinks it is above Millrose's 8.5%.
facts.source_title: Hunterbrook: What Lennar Owes

facts.fact: Platform scale as TPG states it (data to Jan 2026 month-end): since launch in 2020 Essential Housing has originated 850+ projects with $22bn+ of total project value, about 150,000 homesites originated of which about 90,000 already bought back by builders, 16 onboarded builder customers (Lennar the anchor plus 15), across 24 states and 60+ MSAs. TPG reports zero investment losses on any project to date.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), pp. 7-8

facts.fact: Fund ladder per TPG (March 2026): EHF-1, vintage 2020, $1.0bn commitments, Lennar only, 12-month origination period, about $3.1bn originated across about 110 projects, now fully monetised (final takedown done). EHF-2, vintage 2021, $3.0bn commitments, Lennar + 10 builders, 24-month origination, about $9.5bn originated across about 340 projects, in harvest with DPI 1.01x. EHF-3, vintage 2024, $2.6bn commitments, 30-month origination, about $9.2bn originated across about 390 projects by Jan 2026 against targets of about $12bn and 450+. EHF-4, vintage 2026, target $3.0bn+, 30-month origination, targeting about $13bn+ of originations and 500+ projects.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), p. 10

facts.fact: Fund III size conflict: TPG's own March 2026 deck shows EHF-3 'Fund Commitments' of $2.6bn, while IPE Real Assets (13 Nov 2026) reports a $1.62bn final close in 2024 and TPG's CEO said the $2bn Fund IV first close already exceeds the predecessor. The primary figure ($2.6bn) is kept; the gap is not explained publicly and may reflect the manager's own contribution (a $500m GP contribution was reported for Fund III) and parallel/separate vehicles being counted in the deck figure (that explanation is an inference).
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), p. 10; compare IPE Real Assets 13 Nov 2026

facts.fact: Capital turns roughly 3-4x: each fund's originations (land plus development) are several times its equity: EHF-1 about $3.1bn on $1.0bn, EHF-2 about $9.5bn on $3.0bn, EHF-3 about $9.2bn to Jan 2026 on $2.6bn (ratios 3.1x, 3.2x, 3.5x calculated here from TPG's figures; they reflect recycling of takedown proceeds during the origination period and fund leverage, the mix is not disclosed).
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), p. 10 (ratios calculated)

facts.fact: California is about 40% of everything originated: $8.7bn+ of total project value, about 175 projects, 31,700+ homesites in 23 counties since 2020 (through Jan 2026). San Bernardino County alone: about $800m of project value and about 3,500 homesites.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), p. 9

facts.fact: Product definition: 'short-duration' land banking only: land in active development with the first phase of finished lots within about 12 months. Project guidelines unchanged across all four funds: maximum option term under 40 months and average first scheduled lot takedown under 10 months (under 9 months in the 2024 deck). TPG explicitly contrasts this with 'many other land bankers' who hold longer-duration land and need a higher cost of capital.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), pp. 10 and 14

facts.fact: Structure per TPG: builder sources the land and gives EHF its internal underwriting; EHF buys the property and sets a fixed lot price and schedule backed by an upfront cash option deposit; builder develops under a Construction Agreement on a cost-not-to-exceed basis with a completion guarantee (cost can come in lower, not higher); a pre-set monthly takedown schedule that the builder may accelerate but may not fall behind without losing the option; each takedown returns capital plus return. Builder pays EHF's legal and market-study costs.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), pp. 22-23; 2024 deck p. 18 for cost pass-through

facts.fact: Deposit: the 2024 deck states a builder deposit of 19.9% as the 'first loss' tranche; SBCERA's March 2026 staff memo says deposits of about 20% are non-refundable first-loss capital and that the fund holds 'put-back' rights to return a troubled project to the builder or swap in another pre-approved project. The 2024 deck also lists an 'Adverse Development Project Put Back Framework', an exclusive 'first look' on Lennar deal flow, and 'Variable Deferred Land Cost'.
facts.source_title: SBCERA File 26-114 staff memo (19 Mar 2026); EHF III deck p. 13

facts.fact: Positioning on price: TPG told SBCERA its goal is to be 'the biggest, with the lowest cost, and the easiest to use', seeking 'functional exclusivity through price' so that builders show it deals first; it says it would rather win with scale and the lowest-risk assets than move out the risk curve for yield. SBCERA staff described EHF4 as having 'the most attractive pricing versus competitive offerings'. No option rate is published; the only return markers are a 13%-15% target net IRR for Fund III (IPE, Aug 2024) and a 15% IRR reported on the first Lennar fund (Hunterbrook).
facts.source_title: TPG Angelo Gordon Essential Housing Fund III presentation to SBCERA, March 2024 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 24-042), p. 14; SBCERA File 26-114 memo

facts.fact: Underwriting markers from the 2024 deck: average builder-indicated gross margin of 25%+ on selected projects; investment-committee approval for every project; a John Burns market study and IC presentation per project; a proprietary 'Homesite Selection System' software tool given to builders free; standardised documents. Outside counsel: Biskind, Hunt & Semro (Neil Biskind, lead transaction counsel) and Quarles & Brady (Jason Wood).
facts.source_title: TPG Angelo Gordon Essential Housing Fund III presentation to SBCERA, March 2024 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 24-042), pp. 8, 13, 18-19

facts.fact: Fund-level leverage exists: TPG's 2024 process chart has 'lenders' independently reviewing each diligence package and approving the project for a 'borrowing base', and the 2026 risk factors say the fund invests in assets 'with significant leverage' and may borrow at fund level. Lenders, facility size and advance rates are not disclosed.
facts.source_title: TPG Angelo Gordon Essential Housing Fund III presentation to SBCERA, March 2024 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 24-042), p. 19; EHF IV deck p. 28

facts.fact: Cash-flow profile TPG markets for Fund IV: capital deployed on a rolling basis over a 30-month origination period (Q4 2026 to about Q1 2029), peak invested at the end of that period, full return of invested capital by harvest year 2 and wind-down by about mid-2032. EHF-1 DPI was 109% as of Jan 2024.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), p. 13; EHF III deck p. 8

facts.fact: Where it sits: Essential Housing is a credit product, not a real-estate product. TPG's FY2025 10-K lists it as one of three closed-end fund families (Credit Solutions, Essential Housing, Hybrid Solutions) inside TPG Credit Solutions, which had $21.4bn AUM at 31 Dec 2025. TPG's credit platform was $93bn and real estate $38bn of $303bn total AUM at Q4 2025.
facts.source_title: TPG Inc. FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1; AUM split from EHF IV deck p. 6

facts.fact: History: SBCERA's memos say the strategy began in 2020 from talks with Lennar, which wanted a financing partner for its asset-light shift; by March 2024 'over 10' builders participated (11 onboarded, 400+ projects, over $11bn of project value, $4bn of equity across two funds, 59 MSAs in 20 states). So the platform roughly doubled in project value in the 22 months to Jan 2026 ($11bn to $22bn+; calculation from the two decks).
facts.source_title: TPG Angelo Gordon Essential Housing Fund III presentation to SBCERA, March 2024 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 24-042), pp. 7 and 16; SBCERA File 24-042

facts.fact: Team: 27 professionals in 2024 (including open roles) split between a New York capital/investment team (TPG Credit Solutions) and an asset-management team led by Steve Benson (the AGWIP Asset Management entity in Scottsdale per the Lennar agreement). Investment committee in March 2026: Ryan Mollett, Bryan Rush, Paul Grima, Steve Benson and Chris Oka, with Mark Bernstein as investment and transaction counsel.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), pp. 19-20; EHF III deck p. 18

facts.fact: Branding: the 2024 documents say 'TPG Angelo Gordon Essential Housing Fund III' / 'TPG AG Essential Housing'; the March 2026 documents say 'TPG Essential Housing Fund IV' / 'TPG Credit - Essential Housing Fund IV' and SBCERA's memo refers to 'TPG, formerly TPG Angelo Gordon'. The Angelo Gordon name is being dropped from this product.
facts.source_title: SBCERA File 26-114 staff memo

facts.fact: TPG's 2026 pitch shows where it sees demand: optioned-lot shares at large public builders with stated targets (Pulte 70%, Taylor Morrison 65%, Meritage 50%; Lennar 98% post-Millrose) and the claim that Essential Housing is positioned to meet 'the largest builders' capital needs. It cites Lennar management calling the tie a 'unique and very important relationship with TPG Essential Housing'. The 2024 deck labelled Lennar with 'EHF Exclusivity' and showed Forestar (63% owned) as D.R. Horton's alternative land strategy.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), pp. 7 and 16

facts.fact: Fund IV legal vehicle: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV, L.P. (Delaware, formed 2026; GP TPG EHF IV GP LLC; c/o Angelo, Gordon & Co., L.P., 245 Park Avenue, New York) filed its first Form D on 30 Jul 2026 under Rule 506(b) / 3(c)(7): indefinite offering size, nothing sold yet at filing, no placement agent named. Signed by Christopher Moore as general counsel of the GP's manager.
facts.source_title: SEC Form D, TPG Essential Housing Fund IV, L.P. (CIK 2118779)

facts.fact: Fund III legal vehicles and what Form D shows: TPG AG Essential Housing Fund III Holdings (DE), L.P. reported $1,005.07m sold to 12 investors (D/A signed 21 Mar 2025; first sale 27 Mar 2024). Other Fund III feeders per a Form D aggregator: Fund III, L.P. $380m / 5 investors (Mar 2025), SD Fund, L.P. $151.5m / 5 investors (first sale 4 Jun 2024), Fund III (E), L.P. $29.3m / 2 investors (Dec 2025). Sum about $1,566m (calculated: 1,005.07 + 380 + 151.5 + 29.3), close to the $1.62bn final close IPE reported, i.e. outside-LP capital is roughly $1.6bn of the $2.6bn TPG shows for EHF-3.
facts.source_title: SEC Form D/A, TPG AG Essential Housing Fund III Holdings (DE), L.P. (CIK 2015463); feeder figures from formds.com; sum calculated

facts.fact: The March 2026 Form D/A for Fund III Holdings (DE) shows a lower figure than the year before ($489.3m sold, 5 investors, versus $1,005.07m and 12 investors in March 2025); the filing gives no explanation. Fund III, L.P. likewise fell from $380m to $280m per the aggregator. Possibly investors moved between parallel vehicles; not explained publicly.
facts.source_title: SEC Form D/A, TPG AG Essential Housing Fund III Holdings (DE), L.P., signed 20 Mar 2026

facts.fact: Known Fund IV LPs so far (all 2026): SBCERA $150m (approved 19 Mar 2026, about 85 bps of plan assets), Texas County & District Retirement System $200m, Kern County ERA $50m (reported 20 Aug 2026). SBCERA and Kern are repeat investors from Fund III ($150m and $50m in 2024).
facts.source_title: IPE Real Assets, 20 Aug 2026; SBCERA File 26-114; IREI 23 Sep 2026

facts.fact: How to spot its deals in county records: land is titled in per-builder special-purpose LLCs named '[TPG] AG EHC [fund] ([builder ticker]) Multi State [n], LLC', owned by 'TPG AG EHC III SPV n, L.P.', with the Scottsdale asset-manager address (8585 E. Hartford Drive, Suite 118) or the New York address (245 Park Avenue, 26th Floor). Confirmed in government records opened: 'TPG AG EHC III (LEN) Multi State 5, LLC' (Texas TDLR, College Station, registered Aug 2025), 'TPG AG EHC III (MTH) Multi State 5 LLC' (Texas TDLR, Georgetown, Apr 2026) and 'TPG AG EHC III (EMP) Multi State 6, LLC' (Fort Bend County plat, 2026). Reading the bracketed tag as the builder's ticker is an inference.
facts.source_title: Texas TDLR TABS2025026082; TABS2026017834; Fort Bend County plat recording sheet, Talon Ridge Sec 1

facts.fact: Other entity tags seen only in search-result snippets of state/county records (pages did not load, so treat as leads): 'AG EHC II (HOV) Multi State 1, LLC' (Florida foreign LLC, Nov 2021, manager Angelo, Gordon & Co.), 'TPG AG EHC SD (CCS) CA 1, L.P.' (California SOS), 'TPG AG EHC SD (LEN) Multi State 1 LLC', 'AG EHC II (LEN) Multi State 1-4', and a 2026 Florida entity 'TPG EHC E (FSH) Multi State 1, LLC' whose naming drops 'AG'. HOV and CCS match the tickers of Hovnanian and Century Communities; FSH is unidentified.
facts.source_title: Search-result snippets (corporationwiki, bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov, freshfilings); pattern corroborated by Arizona registrations opened on bizprofile.net

facts.fact: 2026 activity signal: AGWIP Asset Management, described as land banker for Lennar, paid $60.14m cash for 132.24 acres / 444 lots near 117th Ave and Deer Valley Road in north Phoenix (near the TSMC site); closed 15 Sep 2026; seller Aroundtown Agua Fria LLC (Vizzda data).
facts.source_title: KTAR News / Phoenix Business Journal item, 20 Sep 2026

facts.fact: Head-to-head with Millrose and Domain: no public statement by TPG naming either rival was found. Its stated differentiation is duration (under 40 months, first lots within about 10-12 months), a 19.9%-20% deposit (Hunterbrook contrasts this with Millrose's 10% for Lennar), rigid takedowns with no pause flexibility in practice, and lowest-cost pricing at scale. Its own chart shows Lennar at 98% optioned 'post-Millrose', i.e. it treats Millrose as part of Lennar's stack while keeping its own first-look arrangement.
facts.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), pp. 14, 16; Hunterbrook 31 Mar 2026 (synthesis)

builder_relationships.description: Anchor relationship. Master Agreement of 8 Oct 2020 created the 'SPV-1 Program': AG Essential Housing Company 1, L.P. buys land Lennar designates and grants Lennar lot options on a set takedown schedule; Lennar pays an option fee (deposit) at closing and Lennar Corporation guarantees a termination fee. Owner equity for the program capped at $1,000m. Dollar figure is the equity cap, not land deployed.

Hunterbrook, from SBCERA materials: Lennar's deposit with AG's Essential Housing fund is 19.9% of land value, max 40-month term, rigid monthly takedowns, termination fee; AG reported a 15% IRR on its first Lennar land bank.

Rialto, CA (Inland Empire): TPG Angelo Gordon bought 41.3 acres for $44.5m in Dec 2023 as land-banking partner for Lennar Homes, which holds the option; planned 429 attached/detached condos ('Renaissance Liberty'). Sellers Lewis Group and Hillwood. Data from Vizzda via trade press.

Ontario, CA: TPG Angelo Gordon bought 23 acres at 13150 Archibald Ave from Lennar Homes for $49.6m (265 planned units); Lennar had bought the site under two months earlier. Article does not state an option, so the land-bank reading is an inference from the seller being Lennar. A second Ontario site (30 acres, $65.1m, 333 units, seller Richland Communities) closed alongside; builder not named.

Palm Desert, CA (University Park): TPG Angelo Gordon 'with Toll Brothers' bought 46+ acres / 169 single-family lots for about $34.3m in Dec 2023. Trade press does not call it land banking explicitly; structure not disclosed.

TPG's own description (March 2026): Lennar is the anchor customer; a 'proprietary sourcing arrangement' / exclusive first look makes Essential Housing one of Lennar's most significant land partners. EHF-1 (2020, $1.0bn equity, about $3.1bn originated, about 110 projects) was 100% Lennar and is fully monetised. Deposit 19.9%. Lennar's share of EHF-2/3 is not disclosed.
builder_relationships.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), pp. 7, 10; EHF III deck p. 13

builder_relationships.description: Sept 2026: AGWIP Asset Management, as land banker for Lennar, bought 132.24 acres / 444 lots in north Phoenix (117th Ave and Deer Valley Road) for $60.14m cash; closed 15 Sep 2026 (Vizzda).

Shows the Fund III Lennar series is at least five entities deep. Builder identity read from the 'LEN' tag.

Texas state record: 'TPG AG EHC III (MTH) Multi State 5 LLC' is owner of 'Vantage Phase 4', 570 CR 140, Georgetown, TX (paving, drainage, water/wastewater; start 1 Jul 2026, completion 1 Mar 2027), owner address in Austin. Meritage as the builder is inferred from the 'MTH' ticker tag; no dollars or lots public.

Arizona registration: 'TPG AG EHC III (NWHM) Multi State 2, LLC' registered as a foreign LLC on 6 Mar 2025; member TPG AG EHC III SPV 2, L.P., 245 Park Avenue, New York. 'Multi State 1' and '4' entities also appear in record aggregators (Phoenix and Greeley, CO). Builder identity inferred from the 'NWHM' tag (New Home's former ticker); no dollars or lots public.

gaps: Option rate / yield charged to builders: not publicly disclosed.
